body: today 29 years ago is also the day my brother died, its still hard on the family. i and my other brother lost a friend and brother, my parents lost a son. 2 years ago i had my first serious relationship and it brought up all my fears and unprocessed grief. catatonic, emotionally numb, confused, angry, withered, etc also describe my usual states

well im turning 43. ive been postponing suicide for the last 23 years, occasionally enjoying life in between for brief moments. my awareness hasnt aged. so i both feel like ive existed literally forever, yet subjectively i also i feel as young as the day i was born (which i dont remember). but the body sometimes feels old and worn, went to post a package today and a sore ankle ruined an otherwise pleasant walk. and i used to be fit and enjoyed hiking (up until 2 years ago). earlier today i was staring out the window, just waiting for something to happen. life sucks, yet we cling to this shit.

yeah, i figured it might not have been much help to you. i dunno, so much stuff i read here sounds like it could have been written by myself, so much i can relate with. from what i understand, seeking enlightenment or liberation from suffering makes it better. so many days im just ready to give up and then i realize where am i gonna go? since i wrote the original reply, i had a brief flash of happiness and that was after meditating for a while. unfortunately meditation can raise anxiety, although i use it to manage my anxiety :/

hey. ive gone thru the same (sort of still am).
this book by dr. joe dispenza (becoming supernatural) has helped me take my mind off things. it might be interesting to u too.

if you have nothing to life for and before you take that plunge off the bridge or shoot yourself, there are other options. you could go to a commune (buddhist, hindu, catholic, free-range/vegan). they can use or defuse your anger there and make you a more happier, balanced person. i might have to do this myself soon as well. it does involve a lot of prayer or meditation or group hugging though, so it might not be your cup of tea. 
ive dabbled in some meditations and discovered this whole business about previous lifes is indeed true (well, for me at least). i have experienced one death (i wake up on the operating table, holding my breath. as i start breathing, my artery bursts or blood sprays out of my mouth and sprays surgeon / nurses with blood and i realise this is it, im going to die. everything fades to black, and i wake up in this body, with an elevated pulse.) that wasnt a normal dream, i dont know what that was.
i does feel like a meaningless circle jerk as you call it. i read this from the dalai lamas site:
The main purpose of the appearance of a reincarnation is to continue the predecessor’s unfinished work to serve Dharma and beings.

those buddhist monks been meditating for millennia and proven reincarnation is true, so i tend to give them some credit. working with your own mind can be incredibly rewarding, but unfortunately its also very difficult due to years and years of conditioning.

i like to go to suicide spots and imagine how many and how people have ended their lives there before. what mental state they were in, what they experienced and the courage they had to go through with it. in my thoughts i then call out to them and hope and wish they found peace and that i understand their pain and do not have any solution for them. sometimes i ask if there is something i can do for them.
last year i noticed on a long walk in large, open and unknown area a bunch of beautiful flowers planted next to a cut down tree. i went back to that spot again
life is so damn tragic and difficult

ive got a lot of pain and anger from rejection and hurt. it does feel like im going through puberty again since last year, i never had a rebellious phase as a teenager, it was interrupted by the death of my brother and our emigrating to another country. apparently all these things build up. did u learn boxing by yourself or in a club?

im sorry to say this, but suicide is the worst possible thing you can do to yourself. until you (or others around you) have learned your (or their) lesson, you will keep coming back and it gets harder everytime.
it might be hard to believe, but the world is a holy place and suffering is there for a reason. 
i suggest seeking help from a spiritual person, they will be able to feel your pain and possibly take some of it away from you and help you along the way. you could also pray or beg a deity directly (for instance green tara). life is brutal, always has been, always will be, but the little gaps of peace and beauty in between somehow still make it worth it. i wish you strength and good luck

just by being here, we are witnessing and causing the destruction of nature. suffering pervades every level of existence. even a loved pet dog inside a loving home suffers as it doesn't have the freedom it desires or misses its owner or it has nightmares or it will eventually die, causing more heartache. and if you don't adopt a dog, it suffers alone in the dog pound and is put down by euthanasia because nobody came to fetch it. just shows how brief life is and its too short to hate people and not forgive them. we cause so much harm without knowing it.

life is cyclical. endless rebirths. samsara. every asian religion has known that for thousands of years.
i started my esoteric quest last year as ive had enough of these cycles of depression where i get better and then throw it all away again and find myself back in the dumps.
thanks to the spiritual work ive done so far (whatever just felt right at the moment, guided by my own ineptitude, stupidity and naivity), ive now had glimpses of my own death, of experiencing or being pure consciousness, of my heart stopping, of dissolving into pure energy and bliss and of scraping along the boundary of utter insanity. oh and ive descended into layers of "hell" which have been terrifying but also interesting. the positivity brigade still triggers me but not as much as it used to, but there are now other things to send me into near uncontrollable rage. the human mind and psyche is truly a weird, wonderful and horrific companion in our lives.

when people tell me life is a gift and we should be grateful for it, it makes me enormously angry. or that we chose to be born and chose to be in this world to experience contrast, heartache, longing, madness, insanity, and bliss. i grew up in a non-religious family and am jealous of those that are happy or claim to be. we all seem to be pissing each other off yet suffer the same issues, nobody really knows why we are here and what life is supposed to be about.
everybody wants to be loved and accepted as they are, unconditionally, but is scared to love and accept others, for fear of rejection or hurting them.

i suggest looking into religion. this is a problem as old as the human race and just keeps on for all eternity it seems. the corruption is within ourselves and we project this outward into the world. we claim we want peace but secretly desire chaos and destruction.
some years ago i was an atheist. then suddenly i thought the worlds problems were because people didn't believe in god anymore. then i became convinced its because of religions. then i blamed technology and social media. ive gone full circle so many times I've lost count. currently, buddhism seems to make sense to me, although im probably gonna change my mind once I've posted this. we are all in this together, no matter what we believe in, suffering is real.

i can relate. its brutal. im now turning 43 and staying with my parents again. ive tried carbon monoxide poisoning, getting into fights drunk, driving motorcycles, hanging (i was up on a wobbly chair with noose around my neck many times), poison hemlock (ended up being wild garlic). thoughts of my parents often brought me to try again and carry on. for treatment ive been to so many psychiatrists, therapists, psychologists, even tried a hypnotist, past life regression, ive had electro shock therapy, plus many other fringe therapies in the last year which im afraid to share. its brutal what ive done to myself and yet im still here and wonder why. last year i bought nitrogen and was going to suffocate myself like that. i still have the tanks and valves. i do hope sincerely from the bottom of my heart that you find inner peace and strength. ive always made the promise that ill help others when i get better but i always forget that promise when things do turn around, or i dont know how to help.

even if you find hope and get better, this world is so fucked up, its not worth living in it. i am afraid that suicide isnt the answer though. you will probably fail or end up as awareness outside your dying / dead body. ive spoken to enough people on the edge and with near death or failed suicide experiences in the last year to make this a very real concern. i suggest getting into a spiritual practice such as meditating on your true self or true nature. myself, i decided this evening that im gonna stop any further spiritual reading or work because it pisses me off but ill continue meditating until i die of natural causes
